title: Texas' Tre Johnson picked sixth by Washington Wizards in NBA draft - NewsBreak
text: The University of Texas' Tre Johnson was picked sixth overall in the NBA draft by the Washington Wizards on Wednesday. Johnson, who wore a suit with shorts for draft night at the Barclays Center, is the Longhorns' ninth lottery pick in the past 25 years and the highest a Texas player has gone in the draft since Mo Bamba also went sixth to the Orlando Magic in 3018. The 6-foot-5 former Lake Highlands High School star, who turned 19 in March, averaged 19.9 points per game in his only season in college. He set the Longhorns' single-game scoring record for a freshman, dropping 39 points in an overtime loss to Arkansas, breaking a record set previously by Kevin Durant. He's only the third freshman to lead the SEC in scoring, joining LSU's Cam Thomas and Alabama's Brandon Miller, who both are having success in the NBA. "Just knowing how hard I work, most definitely, and how consistent I am with it. I'm going do what's been working," Johnson said when asked by ESPN's Monica McNutt what gives him confidence that his game will translate to the pros. "I'm going to keep staying in the gym and putting in those hours. That, so far, has been translating, so I'm going to keep doing the same thing." Johnson obviously wasn't thought of as highly as Cooper Flagg, who went first overall to the Dallas Mavericks, but he's viewed as perhaps the best pure bucket-getter in the draft. He shot 39.7% from the 3-point line at Texas, including a lot of really tough shots as opposing defenses focused on stopping the freshman on an offensively challenged Longhorns team. The Wizards could use him. Washington has had seven straight losing seasons and hasn't even reached 20 wins in either of the past two years. The Wizards traded leading scorer Jordan Poole to the New Orleans Pelicans on Tuesday in a deal for veteran C.J. McCollum, who is on an expiring contract. Johnson will team with 20-year-old Alex Sarr, who averaged 13 points a game last year as a rookie after being drafted second overall in 2024.
